# Boundary to interior: predicting the field from the surface {#sec-interior}

```{python}
#| label: setup-interior
#| include: false
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
from matplotlib.colors import Normalize
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
FIELDS = [("pressure_l2", "pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "velocity"), ("nut_l2", "eddy viscosity")]
# ISLA is the reference configuration (384 x 12, cosine routing, 5e-4, `source_total` query mass), scored by the fleet scorer
# on both interior datasets and reduced in results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json; GeoTransolver-volume is the released baseline
# of the reporting protocol on each dataset.
REF = J("ref_surface_2026-09-23.json")
REFS = REF["summary"]; REFL = REF["lanes"]
def ref_arm(key):
    return {f: dict(mean=REFS[key]["fields"][f]["mean"], seeds=REFS[key]["fields"][f]["seeds"]) for f, _ in FIELDS}
# ISLA's parameter counts on the volume task, from each lane's own config line
lane_params = lambda lane: json.loads(open(RES / f"campaigns_2026-09-22/ref/metrics/{lane}/{lane}/metrics.jsonl").readline())["num_parameters"] / 1e6
ISLA_PARAMS = lane_params("ref_isla_r1_drvol_seed42"); R2_PARAMS = lane_params("ref_isla_r2_drvol_seed42")
# DrivAerML Volume task: GeoTransolver-volume and ISLA with query tokens, 200,000 cells and 200,000 queries per car
RVA = J("ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["arms"]
GTV = {f: RVA["gt_vol_unit"][f] for f, _ in FIELDS}
ISLAV = ref_arm("isla_r1|drvol"); ISLAV_R2 = ref_arm("isla_r2|drvol")
RATIO = {f: GTV[f]["mean"] / ISLAV[f]["mean"] for f, _ in FIELDS}
PAIRED = {f: [g / i for g, i in zip(GTV[f]["seeds"], ISLAV[f]["seeds"])] for f, _ in FIELDS}
# the interior training-car rungs (54 and 109 cars) of the reference configuration
VOL_RUNGS = {54: ref_arm("isla_r1|drvol_n54"), 109: ref_arm("isla_r1|drvol_n109"), 435: ISLAV}
# AirfRANS (interior task): the same pair on 800 training airfoils, 100,000 queries per case
AF = J("airfrans_reduction_2026-09-22.json"); AFA = AF["arms"]
AFG = {f: AFA["gt_volume_1e-3"][f] for f, _ in FIELDS}
AFI = ref_arm("isla_r1|af"); AFI_R2 = ref_arm("isla_r2|af")
AFR = {f: AFG[f]["mean"] / AFI[f]["mean"] for f, _ in FIELDS}
AFP = {f: [g / i for g, i in zip(AFG[f]["seeds"], AFI[f]["seeds"])] for f, _ in FIELDS}
spread = lambda s: abs(s[0] / s[1] - 1) * 100
lead = lambda r: f"{(r - 1) * 100:.0f}%"
trail = lambda r: f"{(1 - r) * 100:.0f}%"
def standing(r, p):
    """Word a ratio with its paired seeds: a lead or a deficit only when both paired ratios sit on the same side of one."""
    if r > 1.02 and min(p) > 1: return f"leads by {r:.2f}x" if r >= 1.5 else f"leads by {lead(r)}"
    if r < 0.98 and max(p) < 1: return f"trails by {trail(r)}"
    return f"is level (ratio {r:.2f})"
```

```{python}
      "result.** ISLA admits its interior queries as interacting tokens and gives them the signed distance to the wall, the same input "
      "GeoTransolver's volume configuration receives. On the DrivAerML Volume task at the reporting protocol (200,000 boundary cells and "

      "at the 300- and 600-lug rungs and ties at 1,200 and 2,400. On Tensile2d it trails at 400 cases with the steeper learning curve. On the fixed-mesh OLBC sets, where only "

      "elasticity set's stresses and displacement (@sec-interior-olbc). Every ratio "
      "is GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA (GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA on the solids), above one favoring ISLA. Protocol: @sec-protocol.")
```

## The task {#sec-interior-task}

A surrogate that returns only wall pressure answers one engineering
question, the forces. One that returns the field in the domain answers the
rest: wake structure, cooling-flow paths, where separation begins. The task
here is the second in its strictest form: predict the fields inside the
domain from the boundary alone. @fig-interior-task shows it on the running
example. ISLA is held to that form. GeoTransolver's volume configuration is
not. It never sees the surface sample. Instead, at every interior point it
takes the signed distance to the full-resolution boundary and its
gradient, which is the boundary information in a different, denser form.

```{python}
#| label: fig-interior-task
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The boundary-to-interior task on the airfoil. Inputs: the sampled
#|   boundary (black dots with normals, as in the surface task) and a set of
#|   interior query points (aqua). Target: the pressure coefficient at the
#|   query points, shown here as the exact potential-flow field the queries
#|   sample. How to read this: the model sees the boundary and the query
#|   positions and must produce the field at the aqua points; on DrivAerML
#|   the field is a RANS solution with a separated wake, for which no closed
#|   form exists, and each query also carries its signed distance to the
#|   wall. It does not show any model's prediction.
#| code-fold: true
Jk = joukowski(n_cells=50)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.0, 3.9))
clean_axes(ax); ax.set_xlim(-2.6, 2.8); ax.set_ylim(-1.5, 1.6)
xs = np.linspace(-2.6, 2.8, 301); ys = np.linspace(-1.5, 1.6, 181)
X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys); Z = X + 1j * Y
cp = Jk["cp_field"](Z)
c0 = complex(-0.08, 0.08); a0 = abs(1 - c0)
inside = (np.abs((Z + np.sqrt(Z * Z - 4 + 0j)) / 2 - c0) < a0 + 1e-9) & (np.abs((Z - np.sqrt(Z * Z - 4 + 0j)) / 2 - c0) < a0 + 1e-9)
cp = np.where(inside, np.nan, np.clip(cp, -1.6, 1.0))
norm = Normalize(-1.6, 1.0)
ax.pcolormesh(X, Y, cp, cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm, shading="auto", alpha=0.6, rasterized=True)
ax.fill(Jk["xy"][:, 0], Jk["xy"][:, 1], color="white", zorder=2)
ax.plot(Jk["xy"][:, 0], Jk["xy"][:, 1], color=INK, lw=1.4, zorder=3)
ax.plot(Jk["mid"][:, 0], Jk["mid"][:, 1], "o", ms=3, color=INK, zorder=4)
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
q = np.stack([rng.uniform(-2.4, 2.6, 400), rng.uniform(-1.3, 1.4, 400)], axis=1)
qz = q[:, 0] + 1j * q[:, 1]
zeta = (qz + np.sqrt(qz * qz - 4 + 0j)) / 2
keep = np.abs(zeta - c0) > a0 * 1.06
q = q[keep][:140]
ax.plot(q[:, 0], q[:, 1], "o", ms=4, mfc=AQUA, mec="white", mew=0.6, zorder=5)
ax.text(-2.5, 1.35, "input: boundary sample (black), interior query points (aqua)", fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
ax.text(-2.5, -1.4, "target: the field at the query points (color: exact $C_p$)", fontsize=9.5, color=INK2)
sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=DIVERGING); sm.set_array([])
cb = fig.colorbar(sm, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.02); cb.set_label("pressure coefficient $C_p$ [–]", color=INK2)
plt.show()
```

**Data.** The DrivAerML Volume task (@sec-datasets): the 435-car training
split and the 48-car validation split used for every DrivAerML comparison
in the book. Each car contributes a sample of the vehicle boundary (cell
centroids, unit normals, cell areas as measure weights) and a sample of
200,000 interior query points drawn from the CFD volume mesh, bit-identical
across every trained run. The volume mesh holds 150 to 166 million points
per car, so even this sample covers about $10^{-3}$ of it and is
overwhelmingly near the wall. Targets are the static pressure, the three
velocity components and the turbulent eddy viscosity $\nu_t$.

**Metric.** For one car and one field $f$ the relative L2 error is
$\lVert \hat f - f\rVert_2 / \lVert f\rVert_2$ over the query points,
with $f$ in training normalization: pressure as $C_p$, velocity as
$U/|U_\infty|$ with the far-field mean included (Frobenius norm over the
components), and eddy viscosity standardized to zero mean and unit scale
*before* scoring. The viscosity denominator is therefore the norm of a
mean-subtracted field, so an eddy-viscosity value of 0.10 is not a 10% error
in physical $\nu_t$: orderings under this metric stand, but the number is
not a physical percentage. The reported value is the arithmetic mean over
the 48 cars (@sec-metrics).

**Protocol.** @sec-protocol, with 200,000 boundary cells and 200,000
interior queries per car. GeoTransolver-volume trains at 1e-3 and ISLA at
the reference configuration's 5e-4. Both are scored in float32 at the
training query count. The arms are not resource-matched and do not receive
the same inputs. GeoTransolver-volume has 27.6M parameters: the surface
configuration's 12-layer, 256-wide backbone plus ball-query local features
over neighboring interior points at six radii. Its tokens are the interior
points only, and each carries its coordinates, the signed distance to the
full-resolution surface and that distance's gradient. Fed the physical
far-field velocity vector instead of the unit direction, it changes by under
2% on every field, so the interior ordering does not depend on the
input-scale rule of @sec-part-baseline. ISLA with query tokens is the
reference configuration (384 wide, 12 layers,
`{python} f"{ISLA_PARAMS:.1f}M"` parameters,
`{python} f"{ISLA_PARAMS / 27.6:.2f}x"` GeoTransolver-volume's),
and its per-slice geometry spans surface and query tokens together. The
parameter difference is stated here once. It could buy accuracy, so the
interior ratios are read as standings of the two configurations as
shipped, not as a matched-capacity comparison.

### How each architecture treats an interior point

| architecture | what an interior point is | what it knows about the geometry | does the prediction at a point depend on the other points requested |
|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume | an interacting token, routed to slices with the other interior points of the request | its signed distance to the wall and the nearest wall normal; ball-query features over neighboring interior points at six radii; no surface tokens | yes |
| ISLA with query tokens | an interacting token in the encoder alongside the surface tokens, with a learned type embedding and routing weight | the relational invariants of its position against the surface anchors, plus the wall normal and the signed distance as a query scalar | yes |

### ISLA with query tokens {#sec-interior-query-tokens}

ISLA with query tokens admits the queries into the encoder as tokens. Each
query is seeded exactly as a boundary token is, from the invariants of its
position, its wall normal and the global direction, plus a learned type
embedding and the signed distance as a query scalar. In every lane of this
chapter the queries also carry the dataset's full-mesh signed-distance
field and its gradient as inputs; the class derives a direction and a
distance from the boundary sample itself, and what the sampled-boundary
geometry costs without the stored field is the measurement of
@sec-nb-internal-geometry-verdict. Each query enters the
measure-weighted routing with a learned weight relative to the surface
measure. The twelve slice layers run over surface and query tokens together,
and the heads read the query tokens. Every invariant is a function of
relative geometry, so rotation and translation covariance hold by
construction (@sec-isla-contracts). What is given up is query independence:
a query's prediction depends on the other queries in the request. The
queries' total routing weight is a learned fraction of the total boundary
measure, split equally over them, so re-representing the same surface at
another refinement leaves the routing unchanged (measure-rescale
invariant). Every standing of this chapter is under
it. The alternative, `geometric_mean`, gives each query the mean boundary
log-weight plus a learned offset. It therefore depends on how finely the
surface is sampled and on how many queries are asked for. The query-count
instruments of @sec-interior-companion were read under that option at the
exploration budget. Nothing else changes: the reference configuration's
width, depth and slice count, the surface configuration's
hyperparameters, no local features.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-interior-200k
#| output: asis
def cell(d, ref=None):
    s = f"{d['mean']:.4f} ({' / '.join(f'{v:.4f}' for v in d['seeds'])})"
    return s + (f" — {ref['mean'] / d['mean']:.2f}" if ref else "")
out = "| arm, 435 training cars, 200,000 cells and 200,000 queries | pressure (seeds) — ratio | velocity (seeds) — ratio | eddy viscosity (seeds) — ratio |\n|---|---|---|---|\n"
out += "| GeoTransolver-volume, 27.6M, 1e-3 | " + " | ".join(cell(GTV[f]) for f, _ in FIELDS) + " |\n"
out += f"| **ISLA with query tokens + signed distance, {ISLA_PARAMS:.1f}M, 5e-4** | " + " | ".join(cell(ISLAV[f], GTV[f]) for f, _ in FIELDS) + " |\n"
out += "| paired by seed, GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA | " + " | ".join(" / ".join(f"{r:.2f}" for r in PAIRED[f]) for f, _ in FIELDS) + " |\n"
out += f"| ISLA, 24 layers (depth variant, {R2_PARAMS:.1f}M), 5e-4 | " + " | ".join(cell(ISLAV_R2[f], GTV[f]) for f, _ in FIELDS) + " |\n"
print(out)
print(": Interior error on the DrivAerML Volume task at the reporting protocol: relative L2 over the 48 validation cars (arithmetic mean over "
      "cars, then over seeds; seeds in parentheses), float32, 200,000 boundary cells and 200,000 interior queries per car, 500 epochs. The "
      "ratio after each ISLA cell is GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA (above 1 favors ISLA); the paired row divides seed by seed. How to read "
      "this: the arms are not resource-matched and do not receive the same inputs (@sec-interior-task); ISLA is the reference "
      "configuration (@sec-interior-query-tokens), and the last row is the depth variant the reference "
      "selection rejected. The AirfRANS twin of "
      "this table is @tbl-interior-airfrans. Data: results/ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json "
      "(GeoTransolver-volume); results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json (ISLA). {#tbl-interior-200k}")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-interior-rungs
#| output: asis
out = "| DrivAerML training cars | ISLA interior pressure (seeds) | velocity (seeds) | eddy viscosity (seeds) |\n|---:|---|---|---|\n"
for n, a in VOL_RUNGS.items():
    out += f"| {n} | " + " | ".join(cell(a[f]) for f, _ in FIELDS) + " |\n"
print(out)
slope = lambda f: -np.log(VOL_RUNGS[435][f]["mean"] / VOL_RUNGS[54][f]["mean"]) / np.log(435 / 54)
print(f": ISLA's interior error against training cars on the DrivAerML Volume task (same protocol as @tbl-interior-200k; nested training "
      f"splits of 54 and 109 cars inside the 435-car split; two seeds). The exponent of the total error over 54 to 435 cars is "
      f"{slope('pressure_l2'):.2f} on pressure, {slope('velocity_l2'):.2f} on velocity and {slope('nut_l2'):.2f} on eddy viscosity. How to "
      "read this: a within-architecture ladder; GeoTransolver-volume was trained at the full split only, so no cross-architecture ratio "
      "exists below 435 cars. Data: results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json. {#tbl-interior-rungs}")
```

Two ingredient orderings sit behind the row. Both were measured at the
exploration budget of 10,000 cells and queries and are stated as orderings
only. First, admitting the queries as interacting tokens, rather than
decoding them read-only from the encoder's final states, closes most of
ISLA's gap to GeoTransolver-volume on pressure, without the signed distance
and without extra parameters. Second, the signed distance closes most of
the rest, most on velocity, and that is what turns the velocity standing
into a lead. A true wall normal at the query (the signed-distance gradient)
is better information than a covariant blend of anchor normals, on pressure
by a wide margin. One caution applies to any per-band reading of these
fields. Far from the body the true $C_p$ has an RMS two orders of magnitude
below the near-wall value, so far-band pressure relative L2 is
ill-conditioned for every architecture. The velocity error, whose
denominator is the far-field speed, is the well-conditioned view of the far
field.

```{python}
print(f"Three things carry with @tbl-interior-airfrans. The velocity lead carries across the two datasets and widens: {AFR['velocity_l2']:.2f}x "
      f"here against {RATIO['velocity_l2']:.2f}x on the cars. The pressure standing does not carry: ISLA leads by {lead(RATIO['pressure_l2'])} "

      f"{trail(AFR['nut_l2'])}. The two regimes differ in what pressure is (gauge pressure on a three-dimensional body against "
      "nondimensional pressure in two-dimensional incompressible flow) and in what the boundary is (a 200,000-cell sample of a car against "
      "a polyline of a few hundred cells). So the velocity lead is a property of how the two architectures treat an interior point, and the "
      "pressure standing is a property of the dataset. Third, the depth variant is "
      f"{min((AFI_R2[f]['mean'] / AFI[f]['mean'] - 1) * 100 for f, _ in FIELDS):.0f} to "
      f"{max((AFI_R2[f]['mean'] / AFI[f]['mean'] - 1) * 100 for f, _ in FIELDS):.0f}% worse than the reference here, the largest depth "
      "penalty of any dataset in the book beside Tensile2d (@sec-interior-tensile2d). The case-count ladder of this dataset, and how the "
      "two architectures' errors fall with training airfoils, are in @sec-compute-allocation.")
```

## Outside the training range: the AirfRANS extrapolation splits {#sec-interior-extrapolation}

**When the global condition leaves its training range, ISLA's interior
error grows less than GeoTransolver-volume's on pressure and eddy
viscosity and the same on velocity, and the in-distribution ordering on
pressure inverts: outside the training Reynolds band ISLA leads by 15%,
outside the training angle-of-attack band by 47%.** AirfRANS ships two
extrapolation splits. `reynolds` trains on 504 airfoils inside a
Reynolds-number band and tests on 496 outside it. `aoa` trains on 804
inside an angle-of-attack band and tests on 196 outside. Both
architectures were trained on each split as on the full split (500
epochs, 100,000 queries, two seeds) and scored on the split's test cases.
The ISLA lanes of this study are the earlier protocol's (192 wide, cosine
routing, 1e-3). Every growth factor divides a configuration's split
error by the same configuration's full-split error, so the readout is
within-configuration and the reference re-run is not required for it.
The readout that separates extrapolation from the smaller training sets is
the *growth factor*: each architecture's test error on the split divided
by its own full-split test error. The bar is the ratio of the two
growth factors. Above 1.10 with both seed pairs agreeing, ISLA extrapolates
better. Below 0.90, GeoTransolver-volume does.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-interior-airfrans-extrap
#| output: asis
AFX = json.load(open(RES / "airfrans_extrap_2026-09-22.json"))["splits"]
fields = [("pressure_l2", "pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "velocity"), ("nut_l2", "eddy viscosity")]
names = {"reynolds": "Reynolds number", "aoa": "angle of attack"}
out = "| split | field | ISLA error (growth) | GeoTransolver-volume error (growth) | growth ratio GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA (paired by seed) | GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA on the split | verdict |\n|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|---|\n"
for sp in ("reynolds", "aoa"):
    S = AFX[sp]
    for f, lab in fields:
        gi, gg, g = S["arms"]["isla_cosine_1e-3"][f], S["arms"]["gt_volume_1e-3"][f], S["growth"][f]
        out += (f"| {names[sp]} | {lab} | {gi['mean']:.4f} ({gi['growth_mean']:.2f}) | {gg['mean']:.4f} ({gg['growth_mean']:.2f}) | "
                f"{g['g_gt_over_g_isla']:.2f} ({', '.join(f'{v:.2f}' for v in g['paired'])}) | {S['gt_over_isla_on_split'][f]['mean']:.2f} | {S['verdict'][f].split(' (')[0]} |\n")
print(out)
print(": AirfRANS extrapolation splits (relative L2 on the split's test cases, float32, two seeds, 100,000 queries, 500 epochs). "
      "Growth = the split's test error divided by the same architecture's full-split test error; the growth ratio compares how much "
      "each architecture's error grows when the condition leaves its training range (above 1 means ISLA's grows less), and the "
      "last ratio is the standing on the split itself (above 1 favors ISLA). Bars: 1.10 / 0.90 with both seed pairs agreeing. "
      "How to read this: the Reynolds split trains on 504 airfoils against the full split's 800, so part of each growth factor is "
      "data-size; both architectures pay it, which is why the ratio of growths is the readout. "
      "Data: results/airfrans_extrap_2026-09-22.json. {#tbl-interior-airfrans-extrap}")
```

Two things travel with @tbl-interior-airfrans-extrap. It is one dataset
and one task, two-dimensional. The HiLiftAeroML regime splits are the
second dataset for the claim and are unmeasured (@sec-limits-regime). And
the mechanism is not measured here. The architecture's premise is that a
model whose learned maps see only invariant scalars, the boundary and a
standardized condition vector degrades more gracefully when the
condition leaves its range than one that concatenates coordinates and the
raw condition into every token. The numbers go that way, but the
territory and routing probes that would show *how* have not been run on
these lanes. GeoTransolver-volume's two seeds also separate under
extrapolation (its angle-of-attack pressure seeds differ by 16%) where
ISLA's stay within 4%.

## Dependence on the query cloud {#sec-interior-companion}

**The interacting configuration's answer at a point depends on how many
other points are asked for with it, so a surrogate built from it is
queried in batches of at least the training count** (@sec-using-checkpoint).
Because the queries route through the same slices as the surface, a
prediction at one point is a function of the whole request. Under the
`geometric_mean` option each query's routing weight also scales with the
query count (@sec-interior-query-tokens). Two instruments establish the
rule at the exploration budget. A checkpoint trained at a fixed query count
and scored at a fifth of it loses more on every field than either margin
against GeoTransolver-volume, while twice the count gains a little. And
fixed sentinel points predicted alone and with growing companion sets move
with the request size, most for eddy viscosity and least for pressure
(results/qcount_reduction_2026-09-11.json,
results/isla_qt_companion_dependence_2026-09-08.json). Training over a
range of counts reduces the dependence and does not remove it, so
query-count consistency is an architectural question. The queries' routing
mass, a learned fraction of the total boundary measure split over the
request, removes the count-scaling of the query weight by construction
(@sec-isla-contracts). The dependence through the shared slices remains. A
read-only decoder whose predictions were exactly query-independent was
built and priced at several times the interacting decode's error, and the
class no longer carries it (@sec-arch-passive-decoder).

## What does not work {#sec-interior-negatives}

**Two mechanisms tested as ways to give ISLA interior context or an
interior prior, other than admitting the queries themselves as tokens,
both fail.** Latent volume tokens placed covariantly along the anchor
normals (769 tokens entering the routing as interacting tokens, with the
requested queries decoded read-only from the result) are worse on every
field than the same decode without them
(results/v0_lvt_reduction_2026-09-07.json). An exact
boundary-integral prior is the wrong prior for separated flow. On the 45 of
48 DrivAerML validation cars whose remesh passes a watertightness check,
exact inviscid potential flow evaluated at the recipe's surface points has a
measure-weighted relative L2 of 4.8 against the CFD pressure, where
predicting zero scores 1.00. The reason is that most of a DrivAerML surface
carries the separated-base pressure deficit that inviscid flow cannot
produce. The learned-density decoder built on those kernels is about ten
times less accurate than GeoTransolver-volume on interior pressure on the
DrivAerML Volume task, and its far-field output decays to identically zero.
ISLA therefore evaluates no exact boundary-integral kernels and places no
latent tokens off the surface.

## A solid: PLAID Tensile2d {#sec-interior-tensile2d}

```{python}
#| label: setup-tensile2d
#| include: false
SF = J("solids_frame_2026-09-22.json"); SFS = SF["summary"]
LM = J("lane_means_2026-09-23.json")  # per-lane float32 means; the tensor-head lanes with the load direction as the one global vector
T2D_FIELDS = [("sig11", "$\\sigma_{11}$"), ("sig22", "$\\sigma_{22}$"), ("sig12", "$\\sigma_{12}$"), ("displacement", "displacement")]
T2D_RUNGS = (32, 400)
def t2_isla(n):
    runs = [LM[f"v2_t2d_isla_r1_tensor_axis_n{n}_seed{s}"]["fields"] for s in (42, 43)]
    return {f: dict(mean=statistics.mean(r[f] for r in runs), seeds=[r[f] for r in runs]) for f, _ in T2D_FIELDS}
def t2_gt(n):
    d = SFS[f"gt512|gt|n{n}"]["fields"]
    return {f: dict(mean=d[f]["mean"], seeds=d[f].get("seeds", [])) for f, _ in T2D_FIELDS}
T2I = {n: t2_isla(n) for n in T2D_RUNGS}; T2G = {n: t2_gt(n) for n in T2D_RUNGS}
T2R = {n: {f: T2G[n][f]["mean"] / T2I[n][f]["mean"] for f, _ in T2D_FIELDS} for n in T2D_RUNGS}
import math
slope = lambda arm, f: math.log(arm[32][f]["mean"] / arm[400][f]["mean"]) / math.log(400 / 32)
r400 = T2R[400]
```

```{python}
#| label: tensile2d-lede
#| output: asis
print(f"**On the first solid-mechanics dataset, PLAID Tensile2d, GeoTransolver-512 leads ISLA at "
      f"400 training cases by {trail(r400['sig11'])} on $\\sigma_{{11}}$, {trail(r400['sig22'])} on $\\sigma_{{22}}$, "
      f"{trail(r400['sig12'])} on $\\sigma_{{12}}$ and {trail(r400['displacement'])} on the displacement; between 32 and 400 cases "
      f"ISLA's error falls faster on every field (two-point slopes {slope(T2I, 'sig11'):.2f} against {slope(T2G, 'sig11'):.2f} on "
      f"$\\sigma_{{11}}$), so the gap narrows with data and is the open standing on the solids.** "
      f"Tensile2d (@sec-data-tensile2d) is two-dimensional elasto-viscoplastic tension: per case a load $P$ on the top "
      f"edge and five constitutive scalars vary, the geometry barely does, and the targets are the displacement and the "
      f"three in-plane stress components. Every mesh node is an interacting query token; ISLA reads the boundary polyline "
      f"with its condition labels, receives the load direction as its one global vector and the six scalars, and predicts "
      f"the stress as a symmetric tensor whose components the recipe reads off (@sec-isla-heads); GeoTransolver reads every "
      f"node with the nodal condition tags in its local embedding. Both models use the reference configurations (ISLA at "
      f"384 x 12; GeoTransolver-512, its parameter match).")
```

```{python}
#| label: tensile2d-ladder-table
#| output: asis
def tcell(d): return f"{d['mean']:.4f}" + (f" ({' / '.join(f'{v:.4f}' for v in d['seeds'])})" if d["seeds"] else "")
hdr = "| training cases | " + " | ".join(f"ISLA {l} | GeoTransolver {l} | ratio" for _, l in T2D_FIELDS) + " |"
print(hdr); print("|" + "---|" * (1 + 3 * len(T2D_FIELDS)))
for n in T2D_RUNGS:
    print(f"| {n} | " + " | ".join(f"{tcell(T2I[n][f])} | {tcell(T2G[n][f])} | {T2R[n][f]:.2f}" for f, _ in T2D_FIELDS) + " |")
print("| two-point slope, 32 to 400 | " + " | ".join(f"{slope(T2I, f):.2f} | {slope(T2G, f):.2f} | " for f, _ in T2D_FIELDS) + " |")
print()
print(": PLAID Tensile2d, float32 relative L2 on the 100 held-out cases at 500 epochs (mean of two seeds; seeds in parentheses), ISLA "
      "with the tensor head and the load direction as its one global vector against GeoTransolver-512, at 32 and 400 training cases; "
      "the last row is the learning-curve slope between the two rungs (error proportional to cases to the minus alpha). How to read "
      "this: a ratio below one is a GeoTransolver lead; only two rungs exist under this configuration, so the slope is a two-point "
      "estimate and not a fitted exponent. The five-rung ladder measured earlier used the dataset's axes as global vectors, an input "
      "the book rejects; it is reported only as the pose-prior diagnostic of @sec-pose-prior. Data: results/lane_means_2026-09-23.json "
      "(ISLA); results/solids_frame_2026-09-22.json (GeoTransolver-512). {#tbl-tensile2d-ladder}")
```

This table measures two things and does not measure a third. It measures
the standing of the general interface on a problem with one global
direction, the load, and six global scalars: a 1.3x to 2x GeoTransolver
lead at 400 cases, the direction the preregistration predicted
(@sec-nb-solids-prereg). It measures the learning-curve slope between
the two rungs, steeper for ISLA on every field, the same ordering as the
AirfRANS ladder (@sec-interior-airfrans) and the DrivAerML law
(@sec-compute-allocation). It does not measure geometry generalization or
discretization invariance, since the specimen shape hardly varies and each
case has one mesh. Those axes stay with the aerodynamic datasets. A
scalar-head configuration with no direction at all fits the training set
and memorizes it (validation error 20 to 60 times GeoTransolver's); it is
the ablation behind the component clause of the output contract and is
reported in @sec-nb-solids-frame-interim, not here. The 24-layer depth
variant is 9% to 27% *worse* than 12 layers at 400 cases on every field on
the diagnostic lanes, so depth does not pay on Tensile2d at this data size
(@sec-nb-solids-tensile2d-verdict).

```{python}
      "stated (@sec-nb-solids-prereg); the 5e-4 lane is the row below. The exponent is the least-squares learning-curve exponent over the "
```

The lug and Tensile2d pull in opposite directions on the standing and the
same direction on the learning curve. Tensile2d's targets are the
components of a stress tensor, which ISLA predicts as a tensor
(@sec-isla-heads), and GeoTransolver-512 leads there at 400 cases. The
lug's target is a frame-free scalar and its loading has no direction of
its own, and ISLA leads. On both, ISLA's error falls faster with cases
than GeoTransolver-512's. The 2,400-lug rung awaits its second ISLA seed
and the width and depth controls (GeoTransolver-256, the 24-layer ISLA).
The standing above is the artifact's (@sec-program-status).

## Boundary data on a fixed mesh: the OLBC sets {#sec-interior-olbc}

```{python}
#| label: setup-olbc
#| include: false
# Every OLBC number below is read from the consolidated current-snapshot artifact: ISLA at the reference configuration with no option,
# GeoTransolver-512 with both released attention backends, and the ablation arms as ratios to the same-snapshot reference.
OLB = J("olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json"); OLP = OLB["poisson"]; OLE = OLB["elasticity"]
OL_RUNGS = (512, 2048, 8448)
PF = "u_l2"
OL_EL = [("displacement_l2", "displacement"), ("sig11_l2", "$\\sigma_{11}$"), ("sig22_l2", "$\\sigma_{22}$"), ("sig12_l2", "$\\sigma_{12}$")]
EL_STRESS = [f for f, _ in OL_EL if f != "displacement_l2"]
BACKEND = {"physics": "physics attention", "flarepp": "FLARE++"}
TRAINING = "training"
def scored(cell): return bool(cell) and "means" in cell
def seeds_of(cell, f): return [cell["per_seed"][s][f] for s in sorted(cell["per_seed"])]
def num(cell, f, nd=4):
    """Seed mean with the per-seed values in parentheses, or 'training' for a cell that has not landed."""
    if not scored(cell): return TRAINING
    return f"{cell['means'][f]:.{nd}f} ({' / '.join(f'{v:.{nd}f}' for v in seeds_of(cell, f))})"
def gt_ratio(rung, backend, f):
    """GeoTransolver-512 (given backend) ÷ ISLA reference at one rung and field; None until both sides are scored."""
    r = rung.get("gt512_over_isla", {}).get(backend); return r["ratio"][f] if r else None
def fmt_ratio(x, nd=2): return f"{x:.{nd}f}" if x is not None else TRAINING
def stronger(rung): return rung.get("stronger_gt512")
def headline(rung, f):
    """GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA against the stronger backend at that rung, with the backend name."""
    b = stronger(rung); r = gt_ratio(rung, b, f) if b else None
    return r, (BACKEND[b] if b else None)
def arm_ratio(rung, key, f):
    a = rung["arms"].get(key, {}); return a["ratio"][f] if "ratio" in a else None
def arm_seeds(rung, key, f):
    a = rung["arms"].get(key, {}); return [a["per_seed"][s][f] for s in sorted(a["per_seed"])] if "ratio" in a else None
def arm_cell(rung, key, f, nd=2):
    r = arm_ratio(rung, key, f)
    return TRAINING if r is None else f"{r:.{nd}f} ({' / '.join(f'{v:.{nd}f}' for v in arm_seeds(rung, key, f))})"
def span(vals, nd=2):
    vals = [v for v in vals if v is not None]
    return f"{min(vals):.{nd}f} to {max(vals):.{nd}f}" if vals else TRAINING
# the Poisson headline ratios (stronger backend) and the elasticity spans per rung
P_HEAD = {n: headline(OLP[str(n)], PF) for n in OL_RUNGS}
E_STRESS = {n: span(gt_ratio(OLE[str(n)], stronger(OLE[str(n)]), f) if stronger(OLE[str(n)]) else None for f in EL_STRESS) for n in OL_RUNGS}
E_DISP = {n: fmt_ratio(gt_ratio(OLE[str(n)], stronger(OLE[str(n)]), "displacement_l2") if stronger(OLE[str(n)]) else None) for n in OL_RUNGS}
E_INTERIM = {n: bool(OLE[str(n)].get("reference_interim_code_v7")) for n in OL_RUNGS}
def rung_word(n): return f"{n:,}"
```

```{python}
#| label: olbc-lede
#| output: asis
p512, p2048 = P_HEAD[512], P_HEAD[2048]
p2048_phys = gt_ratio(OLP["2048"], "physics", PF)
p8448 = P_HEAD[8448]
eight = (f"and {fmt_ratio(p8448[0])} at 8,448 cases (against {p8448[1]})" if p8448[0] is not None
         else "the 8,448-case rung of each set is training")
e_in = " (reference from an earlier code snapshot, interim)" if E_INTERIM[2048] else ""
print(f"**On the OLBC sets, one fixed mesh per set whose boundary is cut per sample into random labeled Dirichlet, Neumann and Robin "
      f"segments with random values, ISLA at the reference configuration with no option leads GeoTransolver-512 on the Poisson set at "
      f"both scored rungs: GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA {fmt_ratio(p512[0])} at 512 cases and {fmt_ratio(p2048[0])} at 2,048, each against the "
      f"stronger of GeoTransolver's two released attention backends at that rung ({p512[1]} at 512, {p2048[1]} at 2,048; "
      f"{fmt_ratio(p2048_phys)} against physics attention at 2,048). On the elasticity set GeoTransolver-512 leads: on the three stress "
      f"components GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA is {E_STRESS[512]} at 512 cases and {E_STRESS[2048]} at 2,048{e_in}, and on displacement "
      f"{E_DISP[512]} and {E_DISP[2048]}; {eight}.** These sets (@sec-data-olbc) are the complement of every other dataset in the book: "
      "the geometry never varies and only the boundary data do, so the task is the pure boundary-data-to-solution map on a known domain. "
      "On the Poisson set ($-\\nabla^2 u = f$ on a square, a random sinusoidal source and four random boundary segments per sample) ISLA "
      "reads the boundary segments with the condition type and value as boundary scalars and every node as a query ($K = 0$); on the "
      "elasticity set (steel, a disc with two holes, prescribed displacement and tractions per component) it receives the prescribed "
      "displacement and traction as rank-1 boundary inputs and predicts the stress as a symmetric tensor ($K = 0$; @sec-isla-inputs-rank). "
      "GeoTransolver-512 reads every node with the nodal condition tags; it is scored with both of its released attention backends, "
      "physics attention and FLARE++, and the headline ratio at each rung is taken against whichever is stronger there, because the two "
      "cross between the rungs on the Poisson set (@sec-nb-gt-fpp-poisson-verdict, @sec-nb-gt-fpp-poisson-512). The 256 test samples of "
      "each set are scored in float32 at every node; two seeds per cell; the 8,448-case rung trains for 120 epochs, the same "
      "optimizer-step count as 2,048 cases for 500.")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-olbc-ladder
#| output: asis
def gt_cell(rung, backend, f, nd=4):
    cell = rung.get(f"gt512_{backend}"); s = num(cell, f, nd)
    return f"**{s}** (stronger)" if scored(cell) and stronger(rung) == backend and scored(rung.get(f"gt512_{'flarepp' if backend == 'physics' else 'physics'}")) else s
out = ("| OLBC Poisson, training cases | ISLA $u$ | GeoTransolver-512 $u$, physics attention | GeoTransolver-512 $u$, FLARE++ | "
       "GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA (stronger backend) |\n|---:|---|---|---|---:|\n")
for n in OL_RUNGS:
    r = OLP[str(n)]; h = P_HEAD[n]
    out += (f"| {n:,} | {num(r['reference'], PF)} | {gt_cell(r, 'physics', PF)} | {gt_cell(r, 'flarepp', PF)} | "
            f"{fmt_ratio(h[0])}{f' ({h[1]})' if h[0] is not None else ''} |\n")
g256 = OLP["8448"].get("gt256_physics")
if scored(g256):
    ref8 = OLP["8448"]["reference"]
    out += (f"| 8,448, GeoTransolver-256 (physics attention) | | {num(g256, PF)} | | "
            f"{fmt_ratio(g256['means'][PF] / ref8['means'][PF]) if scored(ref8) else TRAINING} |\n")
out += "| learning-curve exponent, 512 to 8,448 | pending the 8,448 rung | pending the 8,448 rung | pending the 8,448 rung | |\n"
out += ("\n| OLBC elasticity, training cases, field | ISLA | GeoTransolver-512, physics attention | GeoTransolver-512, FLARE++ | "
        "GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA (stronger backend) |\n|---|---|---|---|---:|\n")
for n in OL_RUNGS:
    r = OLE[str(n)]; b = stronger(r)
    for f, lab in OL_EL:
        ref = num(r["reference"], f, 3) + (" (interim)" if scored(r["reference"]) and E_INTERIM[n] else "")
        ratio = fmt_ratio(gt_ratio(r, b, f)) if b else TRAINING
        out += f"| {n:,}, {lab} | {ref} | {gt_cell(r, 'physics', f, 3)} | {gt_cell(r, 'flarepp', f, 3)} | {ratio}{f' ({BACKEND[b]})' if b and gt_ratio(r, b, f) is not None else ''} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The OLBC ladders: relative L2 over the 256 test samples of each set (mean over samples, then over seeds; seeds in parentheses), "
      "float32 at every node. ISLA is the reference configuration with no option; GeoTransolver-512 is scored with both of its released "
      "attention backends, and **the ratio column is GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA against the stronger backend at that rung** (marked in bold "
      "where both are scored; the backend is named beside the ratio). Top: the Poisson set's solution $u$ along the 512 / 2,048 / 8,448-case "
      "ladder, with GeoTransolver-256 at the full rung. Bottom: the elasticity set per field, ISLA with the prescribed displacement and "
      "traction as rank-1 boundary inputs and the stress as a tensor output. A cell marked *training* has not landed; the 2,048-case "
      "elasticity reference marked *interim* is the same configuration trained on an earlier code snapshot and is replaced by the "
      "current-snapshot pair when it lands. Learning-curve exponents are stated once three current-snapshot rungs exist. How to read this: a "
      "ratio above one is an ISLA lead and below one a GeoTransolver-512 lead; the two backends are not averaged, and a ratio against the "
      "weaker backend is never the headline. Data: results/olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json. {#tbl-olbc-ladder}")
```

### Ablations: per-type geometry channels on the fixed mesh {#sec-olbc-ablations}

**Every ablation is an option added to the reference ISLA and read as arm
÷ reference on the same code snapshot; none is part of the model.** Two
parameter-free query scalars were tested, each derived from one sample's
geometry and condition labels and nothing else. The **per-type nearest
distance** gives each interior query, for each of the three condition
types (Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin), the distance to the nearest boundary
cell of that type. The **per-type harmonic measure** is the exact form of
the same idea: the solution of Laplace's equation that is one on that
type's boundary and zero on the others (the probability that a random walk
from the query first hits a wall of that type), computed on the interior
point cloud with one sparse solve per type per case. On the elasticity set
the types are per component (four measures). Both channels keep the
invariance contracts.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-olbc-ablations
#| output: asis
P_ARMS = [("per-type nearest distances (three scalars)", "distances"),
          ("per-type harmonic measures (three Laplace solves)", "harmonic_measures"),
          ("per-type distances + local relational aggregation (removed option, @sec-nb-universal-agg-lug-verdict)", "distances_local05")]
out = "| ISLA arm on OLBC Poisson, relative L2 on $u$ | arm ÷ reference, 512 cases (seeds) | arm ÷ reference, 2,048 cases (seeds) |\n|---|---:|---:|\n"
out += f"| reference ISLA (no option) | {num(OLP['512']['reference'], PF)} | {num(OLP['2048']['reference'], PF)} |\n"
for label, key in P_ARMS:
    out += f"| {label} | {arm_cell(OLP['512'], key, PF)} | {arm_cell(OLP['2048'], key, PF)} |\n"
def el_arm_cell(n):
    """The harmonic-measures arm on elasticity: the current-snapshot arm where scored; where the reference itself is the earlier snapshot's
    control (interim), the arm trained on that snapshot is the same-snapshot pair."""
    r = OLE[str(n)]; key = "v7_harmonic_measures" if E_INTERIM[n] else "harmonic_measures"
    return " / ".join(fmt_ratio(arm_ratio(r, key, f)) for f, _ in OL_EL) if arm_ratio(r, key, "displacement_l2") is not None else TRAINING
out += ("\n| ISLA arm on OLBC elasticity, arm ÷ reference: displacement / $\\sigma_{11}$ / $\\sigma_{22}$ / $\\sigma_{12}$ | 512 cases | 2,048 cases |\n|---|---:|---:|\n"
        f"| per-type harmonic measures (four Laplace solves) | {el_arm_cell(512)} | {el_arm_cell(2048)}"
        f"{' (against the interim reference, same snapshot)' if E_INTERIM[2048] and el_arm_cell(2048) != TRAINING else ''} |\n")
print(out)
print(": **Ablations, not the reference.** Each row is one option added to the reference ISLA, reported as arm ÷ reference where both were "
      "trained on the same code snapshot (below one: the option helps). Two seeds per cell, 256 test cases, float32; the reference row "
      "holds the absolute error with its seeds. The aggregation row is a removed option and is listed for its measured effect only. "
      "How to read this: these ratios are never the book's GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA, which is @tbl-olbc-ladder's reference row; a cell "
      "marked *training* has not landed. Data: results/olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json. {#tbl-olbc-ablations}")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-olbc-ablations
#| output: asis
d512, h512 = arm_ratio(OLP["512"], "distances", PF), arm_ratio(OLP["512"], "harmonic_measures", PF)
d2048, h2048 = arm_ratio(OLP["2048"], "distances", PF), arm_ratio(OLP["2048"], "harmonic_measures", PF)
d2048x, h2048x = arm_ratio(OLP["2048"], "v7_distances", PF), arm_ratio(OLP["2048"], "v7_harmonic_measures", PF)
agg512 = arm_ratio(OLP["512"], "distances_local05", PF)
if d2048 is not None and h2048 is not None:
    two = f"at 2,048 cases the same-snapshot arms read {d2048:.2f} (distances) and {h2048:.2f} (harmonic measures)"
else:
    two = (f"at 2,048 cases the arms trained on an earlier snapshot read {d2048x:.2f} (distances) and {h2048x:.2f} (harmonic measures) "
           f"against the current reference, slightly worse, a cross-snapshot reading that stands until the same-snapshot 2,048-case arms land")
e512 = OLE["512"]; e2048 = OLE["2048"]
ek512 = "v7_harmonic_measures" if E_INTERIM[512] else "harmonic_measures"
ek2048 = "v7_harmonic_measures" if E_INTERIM[2048] else "harmonic_measures"
hs512 = [arm_ratio(e512, ek512, f) for f, _ in OL_EL]; hs2048 = [arm_ratio(e2048, ek2048, f) for f in EL_STRESS]; hd2048 = arm_ratio(e2048, ek2048, "displacement_l2")
pct = lambda r: f"{abs(r - 1) * 100:.0f}%"
pspan = lambda rs: (lambda s: f"{pct(s[0])} to {pct(s[-1])}" if pct(s[0]) != pct(s[-1]) else pct(s[0]))(sorted(rs, key=lambda r: abs(r - 1)))
el512 = (f"cost {pspan(hs512)} on every field at 512 cases against the same-snapshot reference" if None not in hs512
         else "are training at 512 cases")
el2048 = (f"improved the three stresses by {pspan(hs2048)} and left displacement unchanged ({hd2048:.2f}) at 2,048 cases "
          f"against the {'earlier-snapshot control that is the interim reference' if E_INTERIM[2048] else 'same-snapshot reference'}" if None not in hs2048 and hd2048 is not None
          else "are training at 2,048 cases")
print(f"**On the Poisson set the per-type channel is neutral at 512 cases in either encoding (arm ÷ reference {d512:.2f} for the distances, "
      f"{h512:.2f} for the harmonic measures); {two}. On the elasticity set the harmonic measures {el512} "
      f"(@sec-nb-harmonic-elasticity-512-verdict, @sec-nb-olbc-v11-512) and {el2048} (@sec-nb-harmonic-elasticity-verdict).** A channel that "
      "pays on one dataset at one rung and costs on the same dataset at another is not a universal setting: under the one-model rule the "
      "per-type channel is not part of ISLA unless the current-snapshot elasticity pairs reverse the 512-case reading, and the decision "
      "follows those lanes (@sec-nb-olbc-ref-2048). The local relational aggregation among tokens (each token pooling its 32 nearest "
      f"tokens before the slice routing), which paid on the fixed Poisson mesh ({agg512:.2f} of the reference at 512 cases with the distances), "
      "hurt on every dataset whose geometry varies, did not compound with the harmonic measures on elasticity, and its "
      "polynomial-reproducing variant hurt as much, so both were removed from the model (@sec-nb-universal-agg-lug-verdict, "
      "@sec-nb-harmonic-elasticity-combined-verdict, @sec-nb-local-lpr-verdict). Two diagnostics that break the book's input rules were "
      "also run on the Poisson set, the domain's own axes as global vectors and absolute coordinates fed to every token; both remain "
      "rejected inputs whatever they score (@sec-pose-prior).")
```

## Standing and open designs {#sec-interior-open}

```{python}
#| label: para-interior-open
#| output: asis
print(f"**One architecture covers the surface and the interior: ISLA with query tokens leads GeoTransolver-volume on interior velocity on "
      f"both datasets (by {lead(RATIO['velocity_l2'])} on the DrivAerML Volume task, {AFR['velocity_l2']:.2f}x on AirfRANS), leads on pressure "
      f"on the cars (by {lead(RATIO['pressure_l2'])}) and trails on pressure on the airfoils (by {trail(AFR['pressure_l2'])}), at "
      f"{ISLA_PARAMS / 27.6:.2f}x GeoTransolver-volume's parameters.** The AirfRANS pressure and eddy-viscosity deficits are the open standings on the flow datasets. "
      "Both are seed-robust (every paired ratio below one). How much of them is the fixed pose of the dataset is measured by the "
      "pose-prior diagnostic of @sec-pose-prior, which gives ISLA the dataset's axes as inputs (an input the book rejects) and closes most "
      "of the pressure gap; the mechanism of the rest is open. On the solids the picture is one of targets, "
      f"not of physics: ISLA leads at the small lug rungs and ties at the large ones on the lug's scalar target (GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA {lug_ratio[2400]:.2f} at 2,400 lugs), trails on "
      f"Tensile2d's stress tensor at 400 cases with the steeper learning-curve slope, leads on the fixed-mesh OLBC Poisson set at both scored rungs "
      f"with no option (GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA {fmt_ratio(P_HEAD[512][0])} at 512 cases and {fmt_ratio(P_HEAD[2048][0])} at 2,048, each against "
      f"the stronger GeoTransolver backend at that rung), and trails GeoTransolver-512 on the OLBC elasticity set: on the stresses by "
      f"{E_STRESS[2048]} at 2,048 cases and {E_STRESS[512]} at 512, on displacement by {E_DISP[512]} to {E_DISP[2048]} (@sec-interior-olbc). An "
      "interior decode whose prediction at a point is independent of the request and matches the interacting configuration's accuracy is "
      "a design, not a result. @sec-limits collects the interior limits alongside the book's others. Data: "
      "results/ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json; results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json; results/airfrans_reduction_2026-09-22.json; "
      "results/solids_lug_2026-09-22.json; results/olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json.")
```
